note_claims.claim: Low mood and 8 weeks postpartum.
Low mood for 6 days, starting a few weeks after delivery, characterized by tearfulness, anhedonia, and guilt.
Poor sleep even when the baby sleeps, accompanied by persistent worry.
Intrusive, unwanted thoughts of accidentally dropping the baby, which cause distress.
No urge or intent to harm the baby.
Avoids carrying the baby on the stairs.
Passive thoughts that her family would be better off without her.
Previous depression at age 19, treated with fluoxetine for one year.
Family history of possible postpartum psychosis (mother admitted to hospital with severe mental illness after a birth).
Breastfeeding.
Has had recent panic attacks.
PHQ-9 score is 17, fitting moderately severe depression.
Moderately severe postnatal depression with ego-dystonic intrusive harm-related thoughts and passive suicidal ideation without plan.
Start sertraline 50 mg once daily, which is compatible with breastfeeding.
Referral to the perinatal mental health team due to symptoms and family history.
Inform the health visitor.
Provide details for Talking Therapies, which prioritize new parents.
Review scheduled in one week.
If suicidal thoughts worsen or the patient feels unable to keep herself safe, call NHS 111 (mental health option) or 999.
Seek urgent help if confusion or hallucinations are experienced.

transcript_facts.fact: Patient's age is 8 weeks, but corrects it to ten weeks on Saturday.
Patient reports feeling like they don't feel like themselves, crying all the time, and lacking enjoyment (anhedonia).
Symptoms started about six weeks after the baby was born and have not lifted.
Patient experiences insomnia even when the baby is asleep, and lies there worrying.
Patient has intrusive thoughts about dropping the baby down the stairs.
Patient states they would never do anything to the baby.
Patient has passive suicidal ideation, thinking they would be better off without them.
Patient had previous depression at age 19 and was treated with fluoxetine for a year.
Patient's mother was admitted to the hospital after having the patient's brother and was unwell, hearing things.
Relative reports having had a couple of panic attacks at work.
Chloe's PHQ-9 score is 17, which fits with moderately severe depression.
Clinician plans to start sertraline 50 milligrams once a day.
Clinician notes sertraline is one of the safest antidepressants when breastfeeding.
Clinician plans to refer Chloe to the perinatal mental health team due to her feelings and her mother's history.
Clinician will give Chloe details for Talking Therapies, noting they prioritize new parents.
Clinician plans to see Chloe again in one week.
Safety-netting advice: If suicidal thoughts worsen or the patient cannot keep herself safe, call 111 (mental health option) or 999.
